results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. The calyx is closest to the cortex and receives sensory interneuron afferents. The pedunculus is a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes. The mushroom body lobe system consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?

VFB holds [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain").

results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are sensory interneuron afferents to the calyx. VFB records show that there are [366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, including larval uniglomerular projection neurons and larval antennal lobe multiglomerular projection neurons. The connectome data indicates that these neurons provide input to the mushroom body.

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response: The main components of the central complex are the ellipsoid body, fan-shaped body, paired noduli, asymmetrical bodies, and protocerebral bridge. These components are associated with functions including navigation and orientation, locomotor control, and sleep/arousal and memory-related behaviours.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response:
The [lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111763 "Open lobula plate-lobula columnar neuron LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") is located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind and has distinct dendritic arbors in each lobula plate layer. It detects looming stimuli, which elicits a jump escape response. The LPLC2 neuron projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. There are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe, and they are cholinergic.

VFB does not currently hold data on the downstream or upstream connectivity classes for LPLC2.

results.title: Bidirectional connectivity
results.question: Are there reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) and dopaminergic neurons (DANs)? Which pairs have the strongest mutual connectivity?
results.response:
There are reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons and dopaminergic neurons. VFB found 5 reciprocal class-level pairs between these two neuron types.

The strongest specific inputs to mushroom body output neurons are from adult cholinergic neurons, with a mean of 7.22 synapses per connected pair, and Kenyon cells, with a mean of 7.09 synapses per connected pair.

For dopaminergic neurons, the strongest specific targets are adult cholinergic neurons, with a mean of 2.68 synapses per connected pair, and adult Kenyon cells, with a mean of 2.04 synapses per connected pair. Dopaminergic neurons also connect to themselves, with a mean of 2.51 synapses per connected pair.

The specific pairs with the strongest mutual connectivity between mushroom body output neurons and dopaminergic neurons are not detailed in VFB evidence.

The mushroom body receives presynaptic terminals from [366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neuron types and sends postsynaptic terminals to [304](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPostsynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with postsynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neuron types.
